events.title: Show stderr to the model
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: The harness discards stderr (2>/dev/null), so a failing command shows only "exit code: 127" with no message; in sparql-university the model could not see why its check failed, never validated its query, and finished wrong.
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c003)
@@ -39,7 +39,7 @@

     args = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])
-    result = env.shell("{ " + args["command"] + "\n} 2>/dev/null")  # only stdout: stderr is mostly noise
+    result = env.shell("{ " + args["command"] + "\n} 2>&1")  # stderr too: error messages explain why a command failed
     return format_output(result)

events.title: Tell the model when output is truncated
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: Outputs are silently cut at 1000 chars; in sparql-university the model re-read the data file in pieces, never saw the graduation dates, assumed it had seen everything and answered wrongly.
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c005)
@@ -34,6 +34,9 @@
 def format_output(result):
     """What the model sees of a command's result."""
     output = result.output[:MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS]
+    if len(result.output) > MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS:
+        cut = len(result.output) - MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS
+        output += f"\n[TRUNCATED: {cut} more chars not shown. Do not assume the rest; use grep, head/tail or a smaller range.]"
     return f"exit code: {result.exit_code}\n{output}"

events.title: Explicit work routine in system prompt
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: The sparql-university run ended on reasoning about data counts with the query never executed; the system prompt gives no working method (sparql-university trace, steps 13-15).
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c006)
@@ -11,7 +11,14 @@
 import json
 
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
-Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
+Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary.
+
+Work like this:
+1. Before acting, list every requirement in the task (exact file names, paths, formats, edge cases).
+2. Look at the real inputs first; never guess data, names or tool availability.
+3. Build the result, then test it by executing it on the real data, e.g. run the program or query
+   and compare its output with what the task asks for. Reasoning about the answer is not a test.
+4. If a tool is missing or a check fails, fix the cause and rerun; do not stop on an untested result."""
 
 MAX_STEPS = 200  # a safety net only: the real limit is the clock
 STOP_MARGIN = 5  # seconds kept free at the end

events.title: Show the clock, force delivery near deadline
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: the model never sees the time budget; in financial-document-processor it spent 172 s of 180 s on OCR of one unreadable file and produced no output at all (also build-pov-ray finished unverified), so partial credit was impossible.

+++ agent.py (c003)

 STOP_MARGIN = 10  # seconds kept free so the last command is not cut off
 MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 1000
+WRAP_UP_AT = 70  # seconds left when the model is told to deliver what it has
 
 BASH_TOOL = {
     "type": "function",
@@ -35,6 +36,16 @@
     """What the model sees of a command's result."""
     output = result.output[:MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS]
     return f"exit code: {result.exit_code}\n{output}"
+
+
+def clock_note(env):
+    """Keep the model aware of the deadline; near the end, demand a best-effort deliverable."""
+    left = int(env.time_left())
+    note = f"\n[time left: {left} s]"
+    if left < WRAP_UP_AT:
+        note += (" WRAP UP NOW: stop investigating. Write every required output file/state with your"
+                 " best guess (use placeholders for what you could not read), then finish.")
+    return note

         if not tool_calls:
             return  # the model answered in text: we are done

-            content = run_tool_call(call, env)
+            content = run_tool_call(call, env) + clock_note(env)
             messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": content})

events.title: Show stderr only when a command fails
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: stderr is thrown away, so failing commands return exit 2 and empty or vague output (build-pov-ray: compiler/linker errors hidden, repeated blind retries; financial-document-processor: tool failures invisible during OCR attempts).
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c004)
@@ -39,8 +39,12 @@
 
 def run_tool_call(call, env):
     args = json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])
-    result = env.shell("{ " + args["command"] + "\n} 2>/dev/null")  # only stdout: stderr is mostly noise
-    return format_output(result)
+    result = env.shell("{ " + args["command"] + "\n} 2>/tmp/.stderr")  # stderr kept aside, not mixed in
+    text = format_output(result)
+    if result.exit_code != 0:  # a failure: show why (error messages are printed to stderr)
+        err = env.shell("tail -c 1500 /tmp/.stderr").output
+        text += f"\nstderr (last 1500 chars):\n{err}"
+    return text
 
 
 def run(task, env):

events.title: Deliver early, switch approach, never stall
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent ~25 of 53 calls retrying OCR variants on one unreadable file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray also ended unchecked against the task's wording. The model has no working discipline in its prompt.
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c006)
@@ -11,7 +11,15 @@
 import json
 
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
-Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
+Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary.
+
+Working rules:
+- Time is short (about 3 minutes). First produce a complete, working deliverable in the exact
+  places and formats the task names, even if rough. Only then improve it.
+- If an approach fails twice, or one item eats more than about 5 commands, stop and switch to a
+  different approach, or make a best guess for that item and move on to the rest.
+- Never leave required outputs missing: a best-guess output beats none.
+- Before you finish, check the result against the task's exact wording."""
 
 MAX_STEPS = 100  # a safety net: the time budget is the real limit
 STOP_MARGIN = 10  # seconds kept free so the last command is not cut off

events.title: Periodic progress checkpoint in tool results
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent ~45 calls on OCR variants of one file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray declared done without tracking what remained. Static prompt rules (iter 6) and a late deadline warning (iter 3) did not work; the model needs a recurring in-context prompt to take stock.

+    "which parts of the task are DONE and written to the required place, and which remain. "
+    "If you have spent several commands on one sub-problem without progress, drop it, use your best "
+    "guess for it, and finish the remaining parts first."
+)
 
 BASH_TOOL = {
     "type": "function",
@@ -48,6 +56,7 @@
         {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},

+    calls = 0

@@ -58,4 +67,7 @@
             return  # the model answered in text: we are done

+            calls += 1

events.title: Detect repeated-command loops, force new approach
events.hypothesis: Hypothesis: financial-document-processor spent 25+ calls re-running tesseract variants on one unreadable file and delivered nothing; build-pov-ray also repeated near-identical fix attempts.
events.diff:
--- agent.py (c001)
+++ agent.py (c008)
@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 """
 
 import json
+import re
 
 SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an AI agent that solves tasks in a Linux terminal.
 Use the bash tool to run commands. When the task is complete, reply with a short summary."""
@@ -43,7 +44,23 @@
     return format_output(result)
 
 
+def main_program(command):
+    """The program name of the last command in a pipeline or && chain."""
+    last = re.split(r"&&|\|\||[|;]", command.strip())[-1].split()
+    return last[0] if last else ""
+
+
+def stuck_note(history):
+    """After 4 commands in a row with the same main program, tell the model to change approach."""
+    if len(history) >= 4 and len(set(history[-4:])) == 1:
+        return (f"\n[harness: your last 4 commands all ran `{history[-1]}` and results are not improving. "
+                "Try a different tool or method, or accept the best result so far "
+                "and finish the other required outputs.]")
+    return ""
+
+
 def run(task, env):
+    history = []
     messages = [
         {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
         {"role": "user", "content": task},
@@ -58,4 +75,6 @@
             return  # the model answered in text: we are done
         for call in tool_calls:
             content = run_tool_call(call, env)
+            history.append(main_program(json.loads(call["function"]["arguments"])["command"]))
+            content += stuck_note(history)
             messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": content})
